newsitem.title: USA: N.E. Medical Center to merge with Lifespan-reports.
newsitem.headline: N.E. Medical Center to merge with Lifespan-reports.

text.p: Boston's New England Medical Center (NEMC) will be sold to Lifespan, a nonprofit health care system based in Providence, R.I., according to published reports on Thursday.

The deal must be approved by state regulators in Rhode Island and Massachusetts and is expected to be completed in 120 days. It will result in a company with $1.5 billion in assets, 14,500 employees, and nearly 57,000 patients a year, according to reports in the Boston Globe and Boston Herald.
Terms of the deal were not disclosed and officials from NEMC and Lifspan could not be reached for comment.
Nashville, Tenn.-based Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp had sought to break into the Boston market with the acquisition of NEMC, the newspapers said.
The Herald quoted Columbia/HCA spokesman Jeff Prescott as saying, "We're disappointed with the decision."
NEMC began searching for a partner two years ago. The deal assures that NEMC will remain affiliated with Tufts Unviersity, hosptial officials said.
Lifespan operates seven medical facilities in Rhode Island including Rhode Island Hospital, the primary teaching hospital for Brown University School of Medicine.
